holidays.name: National Poultry Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate chickens, turkeys, ducks and the other feathered birds that fill our farms and dinner plates. Celebrate with a fried chicken feast, a visit to a local farm, or a salute to your favorite backyard hen.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and its origin is unclear. It falls during National Agriculture Week, which fits its farm-fresh theme.
holidays.funFact: There are roughly three chickens on Earth for every human, so they are among the most numerous birds on the planet.

holidays.name: Let's Laugh Day
holidays.description: A day to chuckle, giggle and snort. Swap your best dad jokes, watch a favorite comedy, or just laugh at nothing in particular. Laughter is free, contagious and pairs well with any other holiday.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It sits at the start of spring, when people are ready to lighten up.
holidays.funFact: Laughter is contagious. Studies suggest we are far more likely to laugh around other people than when we are alone.

holidays.name: St. Joseph's Day
holidays.description: A feast day honoring St. Joseph, the foster father of Jesus. It is celebrated with parades, altars loaded with food, and plenty of pastry, especially cream-filled zeppole in Italian communities.
holidays.origin: The feast has been observed in Christian tradition for centuries. In Sicily it grew into the elaborate 'St. Joseph's Table', a feast of thanks for ending a medieval famine.
holidays.funFact: St. Joseph's Day is also the date when the swallows are said to return to San Juan Capistrano in California, though that legend is a Mission-town tradition rather than part of the feast itself.
